correctness.rationale: The published theorem forces \(q_*(T)\ge pK/(K-1)\) when \(K>1\), and \(K=1\) forces contractivity and hence \(q_*=\infty\). For finite target \(Q\), the weighted shift with exponent \(1/Q\) has exact \(p\)-Cesàro constant \(Q/(Q-p)\) and fails exactly at \(Q\) by a harmonic-series orbit calculation. The positive square-zero block has exact constant \(K\) and all finite exponents. Their \(\ell^p\)-direct sum therefore has exact constant \(K\), is \(q\)-absolutely Cesàro bounded for every \(q<Q\), and fails at \(Q\). The direct-sum passage is justified by \((a^p+b^p)^{q/p}\le2^{q/p-1}(a^q+b^q)\) for \(q\ge p\).

value.rationale: The focal paper singles out \(q_*\) as the self-improvement invariant not determined by the optimal \(p\)-Cesàro constant. Determining its complete feasible range at fixed \(K\) is therefore a natural classification rather than an arbitrary example. The result shows that the universal threshold is the only constraint, and that positivity on the classical space \(\ell^p\) imposes no additional gap. It converts two endpoint examples into a full parameter-space description.
